answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 10 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The trellis multiplier is published, charged in shale, and ocean lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 2946 identities would post 3276 proofs and burn roughly 48 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
